anonymous

/uh-NON-uh-muhs/ - the stress falls on NON · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Anonymous means unknown or unidentified by name.

The mural appeared on the bakery wall overnight, and the anonymous artist left nothing behind but a small stencil of a paper crane.

Example

Most scientific journals send each new manuscript to anonymous reviewers—experts whose names are never shown to the author—so that a harsh but fair judgment carries no fear of payback.

Anonymous is more precise than 'secret' or 'hidden' because only the name is missing: the reviewers act openly, their comments are read and answered, yet who they are stays unknown.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unnamed: Unnamed means a name simply is not given in one particular account — a story may quote an unnamed official whose identity many people know perfectly well. Anonymous goes further: the name is not just omitted from this telling but unknown, so nobody reading can supply it.

unidentified: Unidentified means not yet matched to a name — an open question someone is usually still working to answer, like a suspect the police are tracing. Anonymous carries no such ongoing search: the name is withheld or unavailable, and often nobody expects it ever to surface.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

named: openly carrying its author's or owner's name

identified: matched to a known, particular person

Where it sits · how thoroughly the identity is hidden

unsigned → anonymous → untraceable

unsigned vs. anonymous: An unsigned note is merely missing a signature—the handwriting might give the writer away in a second—while anonymous means the identity itself stays unknown.

untraceable vs. anonymous: Untraceable goes a step beyond anonymous: an anonymous donor's name is unknown today, but an untraceable one has left no path that could ever lead back to a name.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — an-: without

Root — onym: name

Suffix — -ous: characterized by

Put it together: An- (without) + onym (name) + -ous (characterized by) = carrying no name. Greek anonymos meant exactly that: nameless. English kept the pieces intact, so the word still reads like its own definition—an anonymous letter is literally a 'without-a-name' letter.

Use the root in a new word: pseudonym: Every thriller on that shelf appeared under a pseudonym that keeps her two writing lives separate.

Word Choice

neutral

Anonymous is the exact word when only the name is withheld: an anonymous tip, donor, or survey. If a person hides their doings and not just their name, reach for secretive—another word in this unit—and if they dodge direct questions, that is evasive. Anonymous people may act in full public view; we simply cannot name them.
